You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

+# go-critic
+
+Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.
+
+![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)
+
+## Description
+
+go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.
+
+## Features
+
+* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
+* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
+* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
+* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description
+
+## Installation
+
+For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.
+
+Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.
+
+It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:
+
+```bash
+go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
+```
+
+On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:
+
+[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)
+
+```zsh
+brew install go-critic
+```
+
+[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)
+
+```zsh
+sudo port install go-critic
+```
+
+## Usage
+
+Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.
+
+Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
+Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.
+
+```
+Supported sub-commands:
+	check - run linter over specified targets
+		$ go-critic check -help
+		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
+		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
+	version - print linter version
+		$ go-critic version
+	doc - get installed checkers documentation
+		$ go-critic doc -help
+		$ go-critic doc

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

const versionString = "v0.0.0-SNAPSHOT"

const helpText = "Usage:\n\n    go-critic <command> [arguments...]\n\nThe commands are:\n\n    check             run linter over specified targets\n    doc               get installed checkers documentation\n    help              shows help message\n    version           shows version of the application\n\nVersion: v0.0.0-SNAPSHOT\n\n"

const versionText = "go-critic version: v0.0.0-SNAPSHOT\n\n"

var commands = []string{"check", "doc", "help", "version"}

func main() {
	os.Exit(run(os.Args[1:]))
}

func run(args []string) int {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, "no args provided\n")
		return 0
	}
	cmd := args[0]
	if cmd == "" {
		return 0
	}
	switch cmd {
	case "check":
		return runCheck(args[1:])
	case "doc":
		return runDoc(args[1:])
	case "help":
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, helpText)
		return 0
	case "version":
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, versionText)
		return 0
	default:
		suggestion := suggestCommand(cmd)
		if suggestion != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "%q unknown command, did you mean %q?\nRun \"go-critic help\" for usage.\n\n", cmd, suggestion)
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "%q unknown command\nRun \"go-critic help\" for usage.\n\n", cmd)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "no such command %q\n", cmd)
		return 0
	}
}

func suggestCommand(cmd string) string {
	best := ""
	bestDist := 3 // threshold is <=2
	for _, c := range commands {
		d := levenshtein(cmd, c)
		if d < bestDist {
			bestDist = d
			best = c
		}
	}
	if bestDist <= 2 {
		return best
	}
	return ""
}

func levenshtein(a, b string) int {
	ar := []rune(a)
	br := []rune(b)
	n, m := len(ar), len(br)
	if n == 0 {
		return m
	}
	if m == 0 {
		return n
	}
	prev := make([]int, m+1)
	cur := make([]int, m+1)
	for j := 0; j <= m; j++ {
		prev[j] = j
	}
	for i := 1; i <= n; i++ {
		cur[0] = i
		for j := 1; j <= m; j++ {
			cost := 0
			if ar[i-1] != br[j-1] {
				cost = 1
			}
			del := prev[j] + 1
			ins := cur[j-1] + 1
			sub := prev[j-1] + cost
			min := del
			if ins < min {
				min = ins
			}
			if sub < min {
				min = sub
			}
			cur[j] = min
		}
		prev, cur = cur, prev
	}
	return prev[m]
}

func runDoc(args []string) int {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("go-critic", flag.ContinueOnError)
	// No flags defined for doc; but need to handle -h/-help automatically
	// flag package handles -h/-help even if not defined? Actually it will return ErrHelp.
	// We need to ensure output goes to stderr (default).
	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
		// For doc, exit 0 and print error without "parse args:" prefix
		// The flag package already printed error + usage to stderr.
		// We need to print just error to stderr (as second line).
		// But flag package with ContinueOnError already printed to fs.Output() (stderr).
		// We just need to print error string to stderr and return 0.
		// However, need to check: For -help, flag returns ErrHelp ("flag: help requested").
		// For unknown flag, returns error like "flag provided but not defined: -x".
		// Original prints that error again after usage.
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%v\n", err)
		return 0
	}
	rest := fs.Args()
	if len(rest) > 1 {
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, "expected 0 or 1 positional arguments\n")
		return 1
	}
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		// List all

func parseGoVersion(v string) {
	if v == "" {
		return
	}
	s := v
	if strings.HasPrefix(s, "go") {
		s = strings.TrimPrefix(s, "go")
		if s == "" {
			return
		}
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ".")
	if len(parts) != 2 {
		panic("invalid Go version format: " + s)
	}
	// Validate major and minor are integers
	if _, err := parseInt(parts[0]); err != nil {
		panic("invalid major version part: " + parts[0] + ": " + err.Error())
	}
	if _, err := parseInt(parts[1]); err != nil {
		panic("invalid minor version part: " + parts[1] + ": " + err.Error())
	}
}

func parseInt(s string) (int, error) {
	// Use strconv.Atoi to get same error messages
	// Need to import strconv
	return atoi(s)
}

func resolveCheckers(enableStr, disableStr string, enableAll bool) (map[string]bool, []string, bool) {
	// Get all checker names sorted
	allNames := getAllCheckerNames() // sorted
	// Parse enable and disable sets
	enableNames := map[string]bool{}
	enableTags := map[string]bool{}
	if !enableAll {
		for _, part := range strings.Split(enableStr, ",") {
			if part == "" {
				continue
			}
			if strings.HasPrefix(part, "#") {
				tag := strings.TrimPrefix(part, "#")
				enableTags[tag] = true
			} else {
				enableNames[part] = true
			}
		}
	}
	disableNames := map[string]bool{}
	disableTags := map[string]bool{}
	for _, part := range strings.Split(disableStr, ",") {
		if part == "" {
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(part, "#") {
			tag := strings.TrimPrefix(part, "#")
			disableTags[tag] = true
		} else {
			disableNames[part] = true
		}
	}

	enabled := map[string]bool{}
	var disabledLines []string
	var enabledLines []string
	for _, name := range allNames {
		tags := checkerTags[name]
		var isEnabled bool
		if enableAll {
			isEnabled = true
		} else {
			if enableNames[name] {
				isEnabled = true
			} else {
				for _, t := range tags {
					if enableTags[t] {
						isEnabled = true
						break
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if !isEnabled {
			disabledLines = append(disabledLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s: not enabled by name or tag (-enable)", name))
			continue
		}
		// Check disabled
		if disableNames[name] {
			disabledLines = append(disabledLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s: disabled by name (-disable)", name))
			continue
		}
		disabledByTag := ""
		for _, t := range tags {
			if disableTags[t] {
				disabledByTag = t
				break
			}
		}
		// Need to handle tag order? For checkers with multiple tags, which tag is reported if multiple match?
		// Original reports first matching tag in checker's tag order? Or in disable order?
		// For now, use checker's tag order (as stored).
		// But need to verify: For a checker with tags [style experimental opinionated], if disable includes both experimental and opinionated, which is reported?
		// We'll need to test.
		if disabledByTag != "" {
			disabledLines = append(disabledLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s: disabled by %q tag (-disable)", name, disabledByTag))
			continue
		}
		enabled[name] = true
		enabledLines = append(enabledLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s is enabled", name))
	}
	// Debug lines: disabled first (in allNames order, which is alphabetical), then enabled (alphabetical)
	// Since we iterated in allNames order, disabledLines are already in order, enabledLines in order.
	// But need to ensure allNames is sorted alphabetically.
	debugLines := append(disabledLines, enabledLines...)
	if len(enabled) == 0 {
		return enabled, debugLines, true
	}
	return enabled, debugLines, false
}

func getAllCheckerNames() []string {
	names := make([]string, 0, len(checkerDocList))
	for _, line := range checkerDocList {
		// line is "name [tags]"
		parts := strings.SplitN(line, " ", 2)
		names = append(names, parts[0])
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	return names
}

func loadPackages(patterns []string) ([]*goListPackage, error) {
	if len(patterns) == 0 {
		return nil, nil

	hasGoFile := false

	var firstNonGo string
	for _, p := range patterns {

	_ = cmd.Run()
	out := stdout.Bytes()

	if len(bytes.TrimSpace(out)) == 0 {

package main

import (
	"go/ast"
	"go/importer"
	"go/parser"
	"go/token"
	"go/types"
	"os"
	"regexp"
)

var generatedRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT\.`)

type fileContext struct {
	fset     *token.FileSet
	file     *ast.File
	filename string
	pkg      *types.Package
	info     *types.Info
	// Checker params
	params *checkFlags
}

func isGeneratedFile(file *ast.File) bool {
	for _, cg := range file.Comments {
		for _, c := range cg.List {
			if generatedRegexp.MatchString(c.Text) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

func parseAndCheck(pkgFiles []string, fset *token.FileSet) ([]*ast.File, *types.Package, *types.Info, []string) {
	// Parse each file
	var files []*ast.File
	var filenames []string
	for _, fname := range pkgFiles {
		src, err := os.ReadFile(fname)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		f, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, fname, src, parser.ParseComments)
		if err != nil {
			// If parse fails, skip this file (but still try to use partial AST? For now skip)
			// Original ignores syntax errors and continues with other files.
			// If err is syntax error, f may be non-nil partial? parser.ParseFile returns partial file even on error?
			// Let's check: If f != nil, we could still use it? But to be safe, skip.
			// Actually for files with syntax errors, original still counts them in checking (N files) but produces no warnings from them.
			// So skip.
			continue
		}
		if f == nil {
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, f)
		filenames = append(filenames, fname)
	}
	if len(files) == 0 {
		return nil, nil, nil, nil
	}
	// Type-check
	info := &types.Info{
		Types:      make(map[ast.Expr]types.TypeAndValue),
		Defs:       make(map[*ast.Ident]types.Object),
		Uses:       make(map[*ast.Ident]types.Object),
		Selections: make(map[*ast.SelectorExpr]*types.Selection),
		Scopes:     make(map[ast.Node]*types.Scope),
	}
	conf := types.Config{
		Importer: importer.Default(),
		// Ignore errors
		Error: func(err error) {},
	}
	pkg, _ := conf.Check("main", fset, files, info)
	// Even if error, pkg and info may be partial; use them
	return files, pkg, info, filenames
}

import (
	"go/ast"

func checkSingleCaseSwitch(ctx *fileContext) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	ast.Inspect(ctx.file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		switch stmt := n.(type) {
		case *ast.SwitchStmt:
			checkSwitchStmt(ctx, stmt, false, &warnings)
		case *ast.TypeSwitchStmt:
			checkSwitchStmt(ctx, stmt, true, &warnings)
		}
		return true
	})
	return warnings
}

func checkSwitchStmt(ctx *fileContext, stmt ast.Node, isTypeSwitch bool, warnings *[]Warning) {
	var body *ast.BlockStmt
	var pos token.Pos
	if isTypeSwitch {
		s := stmt.(*ast.TypeSwitchStmt)
		body = s.Body
		pos = s.Switch
	} else {
		s := stmt.(*ast.SwitchStmt)
		body = s.Body
		pos = s.Switch
		// Skip select? No, this is switch, not select. Good.
		// What about switch with no body? body may be nil? Check.
		if body == nil {
			return
		}
	}
	if body == nil {
		return
	}
	clauses := body.List
	if len(clauses) == 0 {
		return
	}
	if len(clauses) == 1 {
		cc, ok := clauses[0].(*ast.CaseClause)
		if !ok {
			return
		}
		if cc.Case == token.NoPos {
			// Only default
			*warnings = append(*warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, pos, "singleCaseSwitch", "found switch with default case only"))
			return
		}
		// Single case, check conditions
		if len(cc.List) != 1 {
			return
		}
		// Check for break that would break this switch
		if containsSwitchBreak(cc.Body) {
			return
		}
		*warnings = append(*warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, pos, "singleCaseSwitch", "should rewrite switch statement to if statement"))
		return
	}
	// More than 1 clause: no warning (even if one is default? As we saw, single+default doesn't trigger)
}

func containsSwitchBreak(stmts []ast.Stmt) bool {
	found := false
	var inspect func(n ast.Node) bool
	inspect = func(n ast.Node) bool {
		if found {
			return false
		}
		switch x := n.(type) {
		case *ast.BranchStmt:
			if x.Tok == token.BREAK {
				found = true
				return false
			}
		case *ast.ForStmt, *ast.RangeStmt, *ast.SelectStmt, *ast.SwitchStmt, *ast.TypeSwitchStmt:
			// Don't descend into these (break inside them breaks inner, not outer)
			return false
		}
		return true
	}
	for _, s := range stmts {
		ast.Inspect(s, inspect)
		if found {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func checkElseif(ctx *fileContext) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	skipBalanced := ctx.params.elseifSkipBalanced
	ast.Inspect(ctx.file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		ifStmt, ok := n.(*ast.IfStmt)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		// Check Else is BlockStmt with single IfStmt
		elseBlock, ok := ifStmt.Else.(*ast.BlockStmt)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		if len(elseBlock.List) != 1 {
			return true
		}
		innerIf, ok := elseBlock.List[0].(*ast.IfStmt)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		// Inner must have no Else and no Init
		if innerIf.Else != nil {
			return true
		}
		if innerIf.Init != nil {
			return true
		}
		// Check balanced
		if skipBalanced {
			if len(ifStmt.Body.List) == 1 {
				if _, ok := ifStmt.Body.List[0].(*ast.IfStmt); ok {
					return true
				}
			}
		}
		warnings = append(warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, elseBlock.Pos(), "elseif", "can replace 'else {if cond {}}' with 'else if cond {}'"))
		return true
	})
	return warnings
}

func checkAssignOp(ctx *fileContext) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	ast.Inspect(ctx.file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		assign, ok := n.(*ast.AssignStmt)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		if assign.Tok != token.ASSIGN {
			return true
		}
		if len(assign.Lhs) != 1 || len(assign.Rhs) != 1 {
			return true
		}
		lhs := assign.Lhs[0]
		rhs, ok := assign.Rhs[0].(*ast.BinaryExpr)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		// Check op is one of assignable
		var opStr string
		switch rhs.Op {
		case token.ADD, token.SUB, token.MUL, token.QUO, token.REM,
			token.AND, token.OR, token.XOR, token.SHL, token.SHR, token.AND_NOT:
			opStr = rhs.Op.String()
		default:
			return true
		}
		// Check lhs == rhs.X (syntactically equal)
		if !exprEqual(lhs, rhs.X) {
			return true
		}
		// Get original text for "lhs = lhs op rhs.Y" part?
		// Original message shows original source snippet for the whole assignment? Let's get original text.
		origText := getNodeText(ctx.fset, assign)
		// Determine suggestion

		// Check for ++/-- : op is + or - and Y is integer literal 1
		if (rhs.Op == token.ADD || rhs.Op == token.SUB) && isIntLiteralOne(rhs.Y) {
			lhsText := getNodeText(ctx.fset, lhs)
			// For ++/--, suggestion is "lhs++" or "lhs--" (no spaces?)
			// Original shows "x++" (no spaces). For complex lhs like "a[0]", shows "a[0]++".
			if rhs.Op == token.ADD {
				suggestion = lhsText + "++"
			} else {
				suggestion = lhsText + "--"
			}
		} else {
			lhsText := getNodeText(ctx.fset, lhs)
			rhsYText := getNodeText(ctx.fset, rhs.Y)
			// Suggestion is "lhs op= rhsY" with spaces? Original shows "x *= 2" (with spaces around op= and after?).
			// For "x = x * 2", suggestion "x *= 2" (lhs + space + op= + space + y)
			suggestion = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s= %s", lhsText, opStr, rhsYText)
		}
		text := fmt.Sprintf("replace `%s` with `%s`", origText, suggestion)
		warnings = append(warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, assign.Pos(), "assignOp", text))
		return true

func exprEqual(a, b ast.Expr) bool {
	// Compare by printing to string (normalized) and comparing
	var bufA, bufB bytes.Buffer
	fset := token.NewFileSet()
	_ = printer.Fprint(&bufA, fset, a)
	_ = printer.Fprint(&bufB, fset, b)
	return bufA.String() == bufB.String()
}

func isIntLiteralOne(e ast.Expr) bool {
	lit, ok := e.(*ast.BasicLit)
	if !ok {

	if lit.Kind != token.INT {

	}
	// Check value is "1" (but what about 0x1, 0o1, 1_0? Original likely checks value == 1 via types? Or via string == "1"?)
	// From earlier, 1.0 (float) does NOT trigger ++, only int 1. What about 0x1? Let's assume any int literal with value 1?
	// For now, check string is "1" (exact). We need to test 0x1 etc.
	return lit.Value == "1"
}

func getNodeText(fset *token.FileSet, n ast.Node) string {
	pos := fset.Position(n.Pos())
	end := fset.Position(n.End())
	// Read file and slice?
	// pos.Filename is absolute path
	content, err := os.ReadFile(pos.Filename)
	if err != nil {
		// Fallback to printer
		var buf bytes.Buffer
		_ = printer.Fprint(&buf, fset, n)
		return buf.String()
	}
	// Convert line/col to offset? Use fset to get offset?
	// fset.Position gives Offset field? Actually token.Position has Offset.
	// Use fset.Position(...).Offset
	startOff := pos.Offset
	endOff := end.Offset
	if startOff < 0 || endOff < 0 || startOff > len(content) || endOff > len(content) || startOff > endOff {
		var buf bytes.Buffer
		_ = printer.Fprint(&buf, fset, n)
		return buf.String()
	}
	return string(content[startOff:endOff])
}

func checkDefaultCaseOrder(ctx *fileContext) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	ast.Inspect(ctx.file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		sw, ok := n.(*ast.SwitchStmt)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		if sw.Body == nil {
			return true
		}
		clauses := sw.Body.List
		// Find default index
		defaultIdx := -1
		for i, stmt := range clauses {
			if cc, ok := stmt.(*ast.CaseClause); ok {
				if len(cc.List) == 0 {
					defaultIdx = i
					break
				}
			}
		}
		if defaultIdx == -1 {
			return true
		}
		if defaultIdx != 0 && defaultIdx != len(clauses)-1 {
			// Find default clause node for position? Position at default keyword? Use CaseClause.Case pos? For default, Case is pos of "default".
			cc := clauses[defaultIdx].(*ast.CaseClause)
			warnings = append(warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, cc.Case, "defaultCaseOrder", "consider to make `default` case as first or as last case"))
		}
		return true
	})
	return warnings

	for _, cg := range ctx.file.Comments {

			// Only line comments starting with //
			if !strings.HasPrefix(text, "//") {

				continue

			// Exclude go: directives? Check if rest starts with "go:"? Actually text is "//go:..." -> rest is "go:..."
			if strings.HasPrefix(rest, "go:") {
				continue

			// Exclude +, -, !, # at start?

package main

import (
	"go/ast"
	"strings"
)

func checkDeprecatedComment(ctx *fileContext) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	// Check doc comments for "deprecated" (case-insensitive?) but malformed?
	// From earlier: "// deprecated: use New" triggers with casing message, "// Deprecated use New" (no colon) triggers with format message, "// DEPRECATED: ..." triggers casing, "// Foo is deprecated..." doesn't trigger.
	// So logic: Look at doc comments (associated with declarations?) Or all comments?
	// Likely only doc comments (immediately before func/type/etc) are checked, not all comments.
	// Let's implement: For each GenDecl/FuncDecl with Doc, check Doc comments.
	// For each comment line in Doc, if it contains "deprecated" (case-insensitive?) at start? Or anywhere?
	// From tests: "// deprecated, use FuncNew instead" (doc example) should trigger? Let's assume.
	// Need to handle messages:
	// - If comment has "deprecated:" with wrong casing (e.g., "deprecated:" or "DEPRECATED:"), message "use `Deprecated: ` (note the casing) instead of `deprecated: `" (with actual casing?).
	// - If comment has "Deprecated" without colon or without proper format, message "the proper format is `Deprecated: <text>`".
	// Let's inspect more to understand.
	ast.Inspect(ctx.file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		var doc *ast.CommentGroup
		var posNode ast.Node
		switch x := n.(type) {
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			doc = x.Doc
			posNode = x
		case *ast.GenDecl:
			doc = x.Doc
			posNode = x
		case *ast.TypeSpec:
			// TypeSpec Doc is handled via GenDecl? Actually GenDecl.Doc covers? For "type Foo struct" with doc, GenDecl.Doc is the doc. TypeSpec.Doc is for "type ( ... )" with per-spec docs? Need to handle both.
			// For simplicity, handle GenDecl only, plus Field? Hmm.
			return true
		default:
			return true
		}
		if doc == nil {
			return true
		}
		for _, c := range doc.List {
			text := c.Text
			// Strip "//" and spaces?
			// Check if contains "deprecated" (case-insensitive) at beginning of comment text (after //)?
			// From earlier, "// Foo is deprecated, use New" (with deprecated in middle) didn't trigger. So must be at start?
			// Let's get comment body: trim "//" and spaces?
			body := strings.TrimPrefix(text, "//")
			body = strings.TrimSpace(body)
			// Check if body starts with "deprecated" (case-insensitive)?
			lower := strings.ToLower(body)
			if !strings.HasPrefix(lower, "deprecated") {
				continue
			}
			// Now check format: Should be "Deprecated: <text>" (capital D, colon, space, text)
			// If body starts with "Deprecated:" (exact, with colon), then check if has text after? If no text, maybe still warn? Let's assume if correct, no warning.
			// If body is "Deprecated: ..." (correct), no warning.
			// Else if body starts with "deprecated" but wrong casing (e.g., "deprecated:" or "DEPRECATED:"), warn with casing message.
			// Else if body is "Deprecated" without colon, warn with format message.
			if strings.HasPrefix(body, "Deprecated:") {
				// Check if has text after? If just "Deprecated:" with nothing, maybe warn? For now, no warning (correct).
				// What about "Deprecated: " with space but no text? Probably still correct? Let's not warn.
				continue
			}
			// Check for casing issue: body starts with "deprecated" case-insensitive + ":"?
			// Find the prefix up to ":" (if any)
			if idx := strings.Index(body, ":"); idx != -1 {
				prefix := body[:idx+1] // include colon, e.g., "deprecated:" or "DEPRECATED:"
				// If prefix lower is "deprecated:" but prefix != "Deprecated:", then casing issue
				if strings.ToLower(prefix) == "deprecated:" && prefix != "Deprecated:" {
					warnings = append(warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, c.Pos(), "deprecatedComment", "use `Deprecated: ` (note the casing) instead of `"+prefix+"`"))
					continue
				}
			}
			// Otherwise, format issue
			warnings = append(warnings, makeWarning(ctx.fset, c.Pos(), "deprecatedComment", "the proper format is `Deprecated: <text>`"))
		}
		_ = posNode
		return true
	})
	return warnings
}

package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"go/ast"
	"go/printer"
)

func checkParamTypeCombine(ctx *fileContext) []Warning {
	var warnings []Warning
	ast.Inspect(ctx.file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		var funcType *ast.FuncType
		var posNode ast.Node
		switch x := n.(type) {
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			funcType = x.Type
			posNode = x.Type.Func
			// For FuncDecl, pos is at "func" keyword? Original at 2:1 (func). Good. Use x.Pos() (which is func)? Or x.Type.Func? Both same? x.Pos() is Doc? No, FuncDecl.Pos() is Func keyword? Actually FuncDecl.Pos() returns Func (func keyword) or Doc? Let's use x.Type.Func (func keyword).
		case *ast.FuncLit:
			funcType = x.Type
			posNode = x.Type.Func
		default:
			return true
		}
		if funcType.Params == nil || len(funcType.Params.List) < 2 {
			return true
		}
		// Check for consecutive fields with same type that could be combined
		// For each i, if fields[i].Type == fields[i+1].Type (same type string) and both have names, then warn?
		// Original message: "func(a int, b int) could be replaced with func(a, b int)"
		// How to construct original and suggested? Original is "func(" + params as in source? Or normalized?
		// For "func f(a int, b int)", original shows "func(a int, b int)" (without name, without spaces after comma? Actually "func(a int, b int)" with space after comma? Our test shows "func(a int, b int)" (with space). Good.
		// Suggested is "func(a, b int)" (combined).
		// Need to handle multiple fields: e.g., "func foo(a, b int, c, d int, ...)" -> suggest combining all with same type? Original doc shows combining all ints into one field.
		// Simplify: If any consecutive pair has same type, warn with suggestion that combines all consecutive same-type fields?
		// For "a int, b int" (2 fields, same type), suggest "a, b int" (one field).
		// For "a int, b string, c int" (different, no consecutive same), no warning.
		// For "a int, b int, c string, d string" (two pairs), suggest combining each pair? Or one warning per func with full suggestion?
		// Original for doc example with 4 fields (a,b int, c,d int, e,f int, g int) - all ints, suggests combining all into one: "func(a, b, c, d, e, f, g int)" (single warning for whole func, not per pair).
		// So logic: If params can be combined (i.e., there exists consecutive fields with same type), warn once per func with full combined suggestion.
		// How to build suggested params? Combine consecutive same-type fields into one.
		hasCombinable := false
		for i := 0; i+1 < len(funcType.Params.List); i++ {
			if typeEqual(funcType.Params.List[i].Type, funcType.Params.List[i+1].Type) {
				// Check both have names? If one is unnamed (e.g., "int, string"? Actually unnamed params like "func f(int, string)" have no names, can't combine? Probably skip if unnamed.
				if len(funcType.Params.List[i].Names) > 0 && len(funcType.Params.List[i+1].Names) > 0 {
					hasCombinable = true
					break
				}
			}
		}
		if !hasCombinable {
			return true
		}
		// Build original and suggested strings
		var origParams []string
		for _, field := range funcType.Params.List {
			var buf bytes.Buffer
			_ = printer.Fprint(&buf, ctx.fset, field)
			origParams = append(origParams, buf.String())
		}
		// Build suggested by combining consecutive same-type
		var sugFields []string
		i := 0
		for i < len(funcType.Params.List) {
			j := i
			// Find run of same type
			for j+1 < len(funcType.Params.List) && typeEqual(funcType.Params.List[j].Type, funcType.Params.List[j+1].Type) && len(funcType.Params.List[j].Names) > 0 && len(funcType.Params.List[j+1].Names) > 0 {
				j++
			}
			if j > i {
				// Combine fields[i..j] into one: names joined with ", " + " " + type
				var names []string
				for k := i; k <= j; k++ {
					for _, name := range funcType.Params.List[k].Names {
						names = append(names, name.Name)
					}
				}
				var bufType bytes.Buffer
				_ = printer.Fprint(&bufType, ctx.fset, funcType.Params.List[i].Type)
				sugFields = append(sugFields, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", joinNames(names), bufType.String()))
				i = j + 1
			} else {
				var buf bytes.Buffer
				_ = printer.Fprint(&buf, ctx.fset, funcType.Params.List[i])
				sugFields = append(sugFields, buf.String())
				i++
			}
		}

		sugText := "func(" + joinParams(sugFields) + ")"
